title: RADIUS 25 — Build the Combinations
dek: Eight local powers. Twelve working pairs. One region that learns by making.
body:
A roughly twenty-five-mile straight-line field around El Segundo contains an unusual stack: the Pacific edge, aerospace and space systems, LAX and port gateways, advanced manufacturing and industrial craft, universities and research, story and design, sport and live gathering, and thousands of neighborhood operators. But a nearby asset is not automatically a regional strength. Proximity becomes strength when two capabilities can finish something useful together.

RADIUS 25 makes that distinction operational. Its eight powers are described by what they can bring, what public evidence already exists, and the first bounded move each could make. Its geographic doors run from El Segundo and Dockweiler through Inglewood and Hawthorne, Torrance and the South Bay, Carson and Dominguez, San Pedro and Long Beach, Culver City and the Westside, the central university corridor, and the Pasadena research edge. El Segundo is the center table, not the regional capital. The circle is approximate: not a jurisdiction, commute shed, service area, market, membership list, or proposed authority.

The first season offers twelve working pairs. Sea meets space makes a repairable coastal hardpoint kit. Gateways and making test a reusable public handoff case. Making and learning run an apprenticeship relay. Story and sport make a traveling regional game. Coast and gathering turn the elements into league rules. Neighborhood operators apply reliability thinking to ordinary carts, counters, shades, and repair lamps. Each pairing begins with a question, completes one ninety-day proof, names what counts, and offers a one-year horizon.

The browser-local combination builder produces forty routes: choose one of eight starting strengths and one of five public aims—repair and resilience, learning, livelihood, gathering, or connection. Nothing is stored or sent. The instrument returns a working pair, a ninety-day proof, a one-year horizon, and inspectable evidence.

The roadmap has four horizons. In zero to ninety days, show the ring and finish bounded proofs. From three to twelve months, make six real pairs with budgets, access checks, repair doors, demonstrations, and clean endings. From one to three years, standardize only the shared cases, fixtures, proof cards, apprenticeships, procurement, hosting, and league rules that earned reuse. From three to ten years, consider durable governance, space, agreements, or capital only after the institution has been earned through repeated usefulness.

A one-hundred-point strength score keeps evidence separate from applause: existing capacity 20, useful combination 25, open pathway 20, public proof 20, repeatability 15. Leagues, seasons, and open briefs supply invitation and comparison without assigning an entire community one shared role. Skilled work is paid. Hosts can stop. Failures and unknowns stay visible.

RADIUS 25 is an independent PointCast editorial roadmap. No named or geographically referenced city, county, airport, port, military branch, institution, university, company, team, venue, agency, district, or community has joined, approved, funded, sponsored, endorsed, or committed to it. It announces no coalition, event, permit, procurement, program, construction, environmental activity, payment, registration, public data collection, or physical setup.
